record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let Σ be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in the three-dimensional unit ball B^3, and assume Σ is not an equatorial disk. Must its area be at least the area of the critical catenoid K? Equivalently, is the critical catenoid the next smallest-area example after the equatorial disk among immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 10. Let Σ^2 be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in B^3 which is not the equatorial disk. Is it true that |Σ| ≥ |K|?
When n = 3, we simply call it the critical catenoid denoted by K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the closed unit ball. A free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ is an immersed surface $\Sigma \subset B^3$ that is minimal (zero mean curvature) and meets the boundary sphere $S^2 = \partial B^3$ orthogonally along $\partial \Sigma \subset S^2$. Two basic examples are: (i) the equatorial disk $D$, obtained as the intersection of $B^3$ with a plane through the origin, which has area $|D| = \pi$; and (ii) the critical catenoid $K$, the unique (up to ambient rotation) piece of a suitably rescaled catenoid that meets $S^2$ orthogonally, whose area $|K|$ is a specific constant strictly greater than $\pi$.

Question: Let $\Sigma^2$ be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$, and assume $\Sigma$ is not an equatorial disk. Must
$$|\Sigma| \geq |K|\,?$$

Equivalently, is the critical catenoid the next smallest-area example, after the equatorial disk, among immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in $B^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every non-disk immersed free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ has area at least that of the critical catenoid appears to remain open. Related conjectures (uniqueness of the critical catenoid as an embedded free boundary minimal annulus, the Fraser–Li conjecture) are also still open, and recent work has produced new immersed free boundary minimal annuli in $B^3$ besides the critical catenoid, but no proof or disproof of the area lower bound is reported.

status_evidence.title: Free Boundary Minimal Annuli Immersed in the Unit Ball
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a family of compact free boundary minimal annuli immersed in B^3, the first such examples other than the critical catenoid.
status_evidence.claim: New immersed free boundary minimal annuli have been constructed, but no proof of the area lower bound by |K| is given.

status_evidence.title: A Characterization of the Critical Catenoid
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of the critical catenoid via Steklov eigenvalues and Morse index; uniqueness as an embedded free boundary minimal annulus remains conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations of the critical catenoid exist, but the second-smallest-area question remains open.
